Test Scenario: Prepare normal hourly job cards for one day
Pre-conditions: Logged in to app.ptdev.xyz as QA Admin S1 (accounting.export, Access to Reverse = All). Day D within the last 21 days.
Test Data: Day D; a small crew of hourly employees on an ordinary hourly job. Do NOT use Idle Time, Meal or Break job cards (they have no net time or no export line).
Test Steps: 1. Input > Crew Time In / Crew Time Out: paired punches for the crew on D (e.g. 07:00-15:00). 2. Transfer to Job Cards: Dates D-D, Work Crew = the crew, Analyze, tick the crew rows, Transfer Selected > Transfer. 3. View > Job Cards: date D, Work Crew = the crew, Apply. Note the job card count N and the references.
Expected Result: N job cards exist for the crew on D. The Exported column reads No on every one.
Linked AC: E11 precondition: a completed export needing correction

Test Steps: 1. File > Export to Accounting. 2. Tab Payroll. 3. Dates = D to D. 4. Click Refresh. 5. Check Ready = N and the candidates grid lists the N cards as Pending. 6. Click Export N JobCards. 7. In "Export N JobCards to Famous 120.03 via File output?" click Export. 8. Save the downloaded file.
Expected Result: A success toast and a downloaded file. The N cards leave Pending and Ready drops to 0. NOT "Nothing to export". If "Nothing to export" and "Export run created" show together, stop and raise a bug (see E11-F1).

Test Scenario: Confirm the cards are marked exported
Test Steps: 1. View > Job Cards: date D, Work Crew = the crew, switch Include exported on, Apply. 2. Read the Exported column.
Expected Result: Every one of the N cards reads Exported = Yes.

Test Scenario: Find the export on the Reverse page
Test Steps: 1. File > Administration > Restore or Reverse > Reverse Payroll Export to Accounting. 2. Find the row for the export.
Expected Result: The run is listed with Run date = today and time of E11-01, Type = Payroll, Performed by = QA Admin S1, Job Cards = N, and a Reverse button.
Linked AC: E11 step 1: select the export by date and user

Test Steps: 1. Click Reverse on the row. 2. Read the confirmation. 3. Click Reverse run.
Expected Result: The confirmation reads "This will flip N Job Card(s) back to not-exported". After confirming, a success toast shows and the run leaves the list.

Test Scenario: Every card is back to not exported
Test Steps: 1. View > Job Cards: date D, Work Crew = the crew, Include exported on, Apply. 2. Read the Exported column. 3. File > Export to Accounting: Dates D-D, Refresh.
Expected Result: All N cards read Exported = No. Export to Accounting shows Ready = N again.
Linked AC: E11 step 2: every job card returns to exported-to-payroll = No

Test Steps: 1. Input > Job Card: From = To = D, Apply. 2. Open one of the crew's cards. 3. Change a field that must be corrected (e.g. Field or Ranch). 4. Save.
Expected Result: Toast "Job card record saved". Exported to Payroll on the card still reads No.

Test Steps: 1. File > Export to Accounting: Payroll, Dates D-D, Refresh, Export N JobCards, Export. 2. View > Job Cards (Include exported on): read Exported. 3. File > Administration > Restore or Reverse > Reverse Payroll Export to Accounting.
Expected Result: Success toast and file. All N cards read Exported = Yes, the corrected card shows the corrected value. A NEW run (later time) is listed on the Reverse page with N job cards.

Test Steps: 1. Reverse the re-export from the Reverse page (as E11-04).
Expected Result: All N cards read Exported = No again.

Test Scenario: Edit after export blocks the reverse
Test Steps: 1. Input > Job Card: open one exported card, change its hours so Net Time changes, Save. 2. Reverse Payroll Export: Reverse the run.
Expected Result: The reverse is refused for the whole run with "the Job Card was edited after the export". Record as a note (known web divergence M4, legacy allows it), not a fail.

Pre-conditions: A second user with Access to Reverse = User, and one with None
Test Steps: 1. Log in as the User-scoped user and open Reverse Payroll Export. 2. Log in as the None user and open it.
Expected Result: User: only that user's own runs are listed. None: the page shows the no-access message.
